I'm the co-founder of CleanShot, and I'm super excited to finally launch CleanShot 5.0 with Studio Mode and the new Video Editor!

items.title: Murfy AI
items.name: Murfy AI
items.summary: Write, review, and publish to arXiv 10x faster
items.description: Murfy is a team of AI agents for the entire research writing workflow. Murfy helps to write and review your paper in context, fix LaTeX compile errors on the spot, verify reference papers and generate Beamer slides in minutes. Work with unlimited collaborators, real-time editing, free to start.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt!

I'm Shounan, founder of Murple, the team behind Murfy.

Over the past 15 years I've written 10+ papers accepted at top-tier AI conferences (AAAI, EMNLP, SIGGRAPH, IROS), all in Overleaf. Every single time, the research wasn't the hard part, it was the writing. (Here's My Google Scholar if you're curious)

Formatting references at 2 A.M. before a deadline. Chasing co-authors for edits I needed yesterday. LaTeX compile errors with no useful message. Rebuilding the same slides from scratch for every single conference. 

I kept asking myself: we have AI agents now, why is research writing still this hard?

So we built Murfy. Not another AI writing assistant bolted onto an editor, but an agent that actually works through the writing process with you: drafts with you, reviews your paper, revises based on reviewer comments, fixes your compile errors, and builds your Beamer slides.

Researchers in 120+ countries are using it now, and we're growing 50-100% month over month. 

There's still a lot we want to improve, though, so I'd love to hear from anyone who's ever fought with a technical writing tool:

What’s the one part of research or technical writing that you hate doing and wish an AI agent would just take care of?

Tell me in the comments. I read all of them, and they'll shape what we build next.
Very interesting. Do you have a text humanization feature? AI-generated text is increasingly being flagged, so texts - for example, for websites - need to be “humanized.”
How is this different from openai Prism software ?

items.title: OpenClaw 2.0
items.name: OpenClaw 2.0
items.summary: The AI that really does things
items.description: OpenClaw 2.0 simplifies setup by detecting ChatGPT or Claude keys automatically and lets configuration happen through chats with the agent itself. It adds multiplayer team features for sharing sessions, refreshed browser tools for better tracking, and memory upgrades, all while running personal AI helpers locally on devices for tasks like browser control and file management.
top_comments: The team feature seems like the true hero hero here. No one has done that yet. Anyone know if there is a short version of the 55min video somewhere?

Auto-detecting my existing keys is the part I'd push back on. That key is usually already funding something else, and now a local agent that can run terminal commands is drawing on the same balance with no separate cap. Multiplayer makes it sharper, a teammate's shared session spends my quota and I find out at the end of the month. A per-session token budget in the config would cover most of it.

items.title: Murfy AI
items.name: Murfy AI
items.summary: Write, review, and publish to arXiv 10x faster
items.description: Murfy is a team of AI agents for the entire research writing workflow. Murfy helps to write and review your paper in context, fix LaTeX compile errors on the spot, verify reference papers and generate Beamer slides in minutes. Work with unlimited collaborators, real-time editing, free to start.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt!

I'm Shounan, founder of Murple, the team behind Murfy.

Over the past 15 years I've written 10+ papers accepted at top-tier AI conferences (AAAI, EMNLP, SIGGRAPH, IROS), all in Overleaf. Every single time, the research wasn't the hard part, it was the writing. (Here's My Google Scholar if you're curious)

Formatting references at 2 A.M. before a deadline. Chasing co-authors for edits I needed yesterday. LaTeX compile errors with no useful message. Rebuilding the same slides from scratch for every single conference. 

I kept asking myself: we have AI agents now, why is research writing still this hard?

So we built Murfy. Not another AI writing assistant bolted onto an editor, but an agent that actually works through the writing process with you: drafts with you, reviews your paper, revises based on reviewer comments, fixes your compile errors, and builds your Beamer slides.

Researchers in 120+ countries are using it now, and we're growing 50-100% month over month. 

There's still a lot we want to improve, though, so I'd love to hear from anyone who's ever fought with a technical writing tool:

What’s the one part of research or technical writing that you hate doing and wish an AI agent would just take care of?

Tell me in the comments. I read all of them, and they'll shape what we build next.
Very interesting. Do you have a text humanization feature? AI-generated text is increasingly being flagged, so texts - for example, for websites - need to be “humanized.”
How is this different from openai Prism software ?

items.title: OpenClaw 2.0
items.name: OpenClaw 2.0
items.summary: The AI that really does things
items.description: OpenClaw 2.0 simplifies setup by detecting ChatGPT or Claude keys automatically and lets configuration happen through chats with the agent itself. It adds multiplayer team features for sharing sessions, refreshed browser tools for better tracking, and memory upgrades, all while running personal AI helpers locally on devices for tasks like browser control and file management.
top_comments: The team feature seems like the true hero hero here. No one has done that yet. Anyone know if there is a short version of the 55min video somewhere?

Auto-detecting my existing keys is the part I'd push back on. That key is usually already funding something else, and now a local agent that can run terminal commands is drawing on the same balance with no separate cap. Multiplayer makes it sharper, a teammate's shared session spends my quota and I find out at the end of the month. A per-session token budget in the config would cover most of it.

high_potential_items.reuse_direction: 可借鉴其将新闻、地缘事件与基础设施状态汇成单屏态势视图的做法，用于行业风险监控或区域安全分析产品。

high_potential_items.ai_rationale: 实时全球情报监测AI仪表盘，用户量巨大且近期有版本更新，具备AI数据应用代表性，设为headline。

high_potential_items.title: jo-inc/camofox-browser
high_potential_items.name: camofox-browser
high_potential_items.summary: Stealth headless browser for AI agents — bypass Cloudflare, bot detection, and anti-scraping. Drop-in Puppeteer/Playwright replacement.
high_potential_items.reuse_direction: 借鉴其隐身伪装技术，打造面向AI代理的抗反爬浏览器自动化工具。
high_potential_items.minimal_mvp: 先实现隐身伪装核心，跑通绕过Cloudflare访问页面并返回HTML的最小流程。
high_potential_items.ai_rationale: 作为AI Agent绕过反爬的专用无头浏览器，与自动化工作流高度契合，工具属性强且社区验证充分，值得high。

high_potential_items.title: sansan0/TrendRadar
high_potential_items.name: trendradar
high_potential_items.summary: ⭐AI-driven public opinion & trend monitor with multi-platform aggregation, RSS, and smart alerts.🎯 告别信息过载，你的 AI 舆情监控助手与热点筛选工具！聚合多平台热点 + RSS 订阅，支持关键词精准筛选。AI 智能筛选新闻 + AI 翻译 + AI 分析简报直推手机，也支持接入 MCP 架构，赋能 AI 自然语言对话分析、情感洞察与趋势预测等。支持 Docker ，数据本地/云端自持。集成微信/飞书/钉钉/Telegram/邮件/ntfy/bark/slack 等渠道智能推送。
high_potential_items.reuse_direction: 借鉴其将多平台信息源聚合后经LLM筛选并推送至IM的产品形态，做轻量级情报订阅工具。
high_potential_items.minimal_mvp: 先抓取几个RSS源，调用LLM按关键词筛选，把结果推送到Telegram即可。
high_potential_items.ai_rationale: AI热点监控与聚合产品，契合数据智能方向，但产品形态与上一项重叠，关注度中等。

high_potential_items.title: HBAI-Ltd/Toonflow-app
high_potential_items.name: toonflow-app
high_potential_items.summary: Toonflow 是开源一站式 AI 短剧创作工具，将小说、剧本快速转化为动画短剧。集成 AI 编剧、智能分镜、角色与视频生成，跨平台桌面端轻量部署，助力创作者低成本批量产出视觉内容。Toonflow is an open-source AI tool that turns stories and scripts into animated short dramas. Features AI scriptwriting, storyboarding, character and video generation. A cross-platform desktop app for efficient content creation.
high_potential_items.highlight_one_liner: 小说剧本一键生成动画短剧
high_potential_items.reuse_direction: 把文本剧本自动转成动画短剧的流水线，重点在于AI编剧到分镜、角色、视频生成的一体化串联。
high_potential_items.minimal_mvp: 第一版实现输入一段剧本，自动生成分镜脚本和角色设定，并渲染出几秒钟的动画片段。
high_potential_items.ai_rationale: 面向短剧创作的内容生成工具并非法律/供应链/教育等重点关注领域，匹配度低，按low处理。

interest_sections.title: 简历优化助手
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 xiaohongshu、GitHub：求职者反馈不具体的核心是‘不会按岗位改经历’，因此以JD关键词为前提、能落到每句话的AI改写与提示比单纯模板检查更有价值。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 求职者最缺的不是通用模板，而是拿到目标岗位JD后仍不知道具体怎么把自己的经历改成与岗位关键词匹配、带量化结果的表达

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在按HR反感点逐条自查、圈出5-10个JD高频词后重写经历结构（如公司/岗位/时间+动作+效果），也有人开始尝试GitHub上的JobPilot等AI简历工具。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得继续跟踪把‘JD关键词→逐段经历改写建议→量化结果’做成自动化反馈的简历优化方向，让用户不用自己对照清单检查每一句。

interest_sections.title: 供应链分析 Agent
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 xiaohongshu、GitHub，供应链补货决策仍停留在个人经验与手工预警，Agent 的机会在于把备货时点与数量判断规则化、场景化。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前大家在社媒上用简易备货公式讨论再订货点和订货批量，主要靠 Excel/经验贴推算；开源侧 DecisionAgent 只给出通用多场景决策架构，尚未落到供应链补货场景。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪将再订货点预警与补货数量测算做成可解释的供应链决策 Agent，输入库存和销售数据后按品类/供应商周期给出触发补货的时间点和建议采购量，并不断权衡缺货成本与仓储费。
